newsitem.title: USA: January U.S. auto sales rise from year ago.
newsitem.headline: January U.S. auto sales rise from year ago.

text.p: U.S. car and light truck sales during the month of January totalled 1,091,980 with all automakers reporting, a 6.3 percent increase on a daily sales rate from 1,027,571 sold a year earlier.
The seasonally adjusted annual sales rate for January was 15.5 million units, up from 14 million a year ago, when East Coast blizzards kept buyers out of showrooms.

The U.S. Big Three automakers lost ground in the market share battle as Japanese automakers made gains, prompting complaints from some in the U.S. auto industry that the U.S. dollar's strength against the yen is making it harder for U.S. automakers to compete.
Detroit's Big Three ended January with 71 percent of the U.S. market, down from 74.73 percent a year ago. All Japanese automakers had 24.54 percent, versus 21.18 percent in January 1996.

The following chart represents U.S. sales of cars and trucks and market shares for the month of January, as reported by individual automakers. The chart was delayed because Mercedes-Benz reported sales later than normal.
